accountantMode.label: Accountant Mode
accountantMode.toggleTitle: Tap to change — an explanation appears before anything is applied
accountantMode.turnOffMessage: Accountant Mode is currently ON. Turning it off hides the accounting menus — Transaction Records (journal), Details by Account (general ledger), Chart of Accounts — and the debit/credit labels on forms, so the screen speaks everyday language only (money in / money out). This changes only YOUR view: not the data, the figures, or your access rights. You can turn it back on at any time.
accountantMode.turnOnMessage: Accountant Mode is currently OFF. Turning it on shows the accounting menus — Transaction Records (journal), Details by Account (general ledger), Chart of Accounts — and the debit/credit labels on forms. Useful if you know bookkeeping. This changes only YOUR view: not the data, the figures, or your access rights. You can turn it off again at any time.

contracts.title: Contracts ({count})
contracts.learnMoreList: Learn about this: what a sales contract is
contracts.learnMoreNew: Learn about this: what a contract is
contracts.searchPlaceholder: Search contract no., buyer, or consignee...
contracts.emptyDescription: Create the first contract before any goods are shipped.
contracts.createDescription: Fill in the essentials first: number, date, buyer, and the goods. Payment terms, packaging, and shipment sit under “Full details” and may be skipped.
contracts.detailsHint: The fields every contract needs. The rest sit under “Full details” below.
contracts.rateHintNew: Required — the rate is stored on the contract and used for its IDR value in the ledger.
contracts.rateHintEdit: Stored on the contract — the journal is reversed and reposted using this rate.
contracts.advancedDescription: Due date, consignee, packaging, shipment, payment terms, and status. Skippable — all optional.
contracts.top1Hint: Free text from the agreement, e.g. “30% advance”. Not a date — for dates, use the Due Date field above.
contracts.saveFailed: The contract could not be saved yet.
contracts.deleteMessage: This contract and its payments will be deleted, and the journals they created reversed in the same transaction. This cannot be undone. If the contract fell through but you want to keep its history, just change its status to "Cancelled".
contracts.chainDescription: This contract's journey: shipped on delivery orders, billed on invoices, then paid. Payment figures are summed in IDR (the ledger base value).
contracts.outstandingDescription: How many kilograms of each item have shipped and been invoiced, and how much is left. That remainder is what an invoice pulls in automatically.
contracts.emptyLinesTitle: This contract has no item lines yet
contracts.emptyLinesDescription: Without item lines there is nothing to ship or invoice. Add the goods via Edit.
contracts.unmatchedBoth: Some document lines name goods that are not on this contract — delivery orders {delivered} kg — invoices {invoiced} kg. Those lines do not count towards fulfilling the contract.
contracts.unmatchedDelivery: Some document lines name goods that are not on this contract — delivery orders {delivered} kg. Those lines do not count towards fulfilling the contract.
contracts.unmatchedInvoice: Some document lines name goods that are not on this contract — invoices {invoiced} kg. Those lines do not count towards fulfilling the contract.
contracts.noInvoices: No invoices from this contract yet.
contracts.emptyPaymentsDescription: No advance or settlement has been recorded for this contract yet. Record the first one with the form above.
contracts.updateFailed: Failed to save the contract changes

invoices.title: Sales Invoices ({count})
invoices.learnMore: Learn about this: what a sales invoice is
invoices.emptyDescription: Record your first sale — the flow guides you step by step.
invoices.createDescriptionBefore: Type it in by hand, or pull it ("Ambil") from a contract so the goods, remaining quantities, and prices fill themselves in. Once saved, the balance shows up under “Unpaid by Customers” until it is settled. First time? The guided flow is easier:
invoices.pullDescriptionA: Pick the source contract, then pull its goods across. What comes over is the
invoices.pullDescriptionB: that has not been invoiced — so nothing can be billed twice.
invoices.noContractLines: This contract has no item lines yet.
invoices.loadOutstandingFailed: Failed to load the contract remainder.
invoices.pullNoneDelivery: Nothing has shipped that is still waiting to be invoiced.
invoices.pullNoneContract: Every item on this contract has already been invoiced.
invoices.pullNote: {count} lines pulled from {source} {contractNo}. Quantities may be reduced, never raised above the remainder.
invoices.lineRemainingOver: Contract remainder {kg} kg — over the remainder, the invoice will be rejected!
invoices.lineOutsideContract: Outside the contract's lines — not capped by any remainder.
invoices.advancedDescription: Due date, status, currency & rate, VAT, and export papers (PEB). An ordinary rupiah invoice uses the defaults and need not open this.
invoices.overContractMessage: The quantity being invoiced exceeds the contract remainder: {lines}. Reduce it to the remainder, or raise a new contract for the excess.
invoices.saveFailed: The invoice could not be saved yet.
invoices.deleteMessage: This invoice and its payments will be deleted, and the journals they created reversed in the same transaction — including the receivable and its output VAT. This cannot be undone. If the invoice fell through but you want to keep its history, just change its status to "Cancelled".
invoices.emptyPaymentsDescription: The whole value of this invoice is still recorded as a receivable. Record the first payment with the form above.
invoices.updateFailed: Failed to save the invoice changes

sales.title: Record a Sale
sales.descriptionA: Guided step by step: customer, goods, shipment, then the invoice. Move back and forth as you like —
sales.descriptionB: until you press “Finish & Save” on the last step.
sales.savedHint: Every document below was created together in a single save.
sales.outstandingLoadFailed: The contract remainder failed to load. You can still enter the goods by hand.
sales.saveFailed: The sale could not be saved yet.
sales.pullNoneContract: Every item on this contract has already been invoiced.
sales.pullNote: {count} lines pulled from the remainder of contract {contractNo}. Quantities may be reduced, never raised above the remainder.
sales.pullDescription: If this sale bills an existing contract, pick it here: the goods, remaining quantities, and prices fill themselves in, and the invoice cannot exceed the contract remainder.
sales.lineNoStockItem: This item is not in the stock list, so no delivery order can be issued for it. The invoice can still be raised.
sales.lineStockAndRemaining: Stock available {stock} kg · contract remainder {remaining} kg
sales.lineStockAndRemainingOver: Stock available {stock} kg · contract remainder {remaining} kg — over the contract remainder!
sales.shipCheckboxA: The goods have shipped — issue a
sales.shipCheckboxHint: A delivery order reduces stock and posts the cost-of-goods journal. If nothing has left yet, leave this unticked and carry on — the delivery order can be issued later.
sales.emptyStockDescription: A delivery order reduces stock, so the goods must be recorded first.
sales.shipStockOverStock: Stock available {stock} kg — over stock, the delivery order will be rejected!
sales.shipStockOverOrder: Stock available {stock} kg — more than the quantity ordered!
sales.shipStockOverBoth: Stock available {stock} kg — over stock, the delivery order will be rejected! — more than the quantity ordered!
sales.deliveryAdvancedDescription: Vehicle number, container number, and shipping notes.
sales.billedHint: Quantities are pulled from the previous steps, not retyped. Reduce them if only part is being billed now.
sales.invoiceAdvancedDescription: Due date, currency & rate, and VAT. An ordinary rupiah invoice uses the defaults and need not open this.
sales.deliveryHint: Dated {date} — stock is reduced and the cost-of-goods journal is posted.
sales.summaryFooter: Once saved, the unpaid balance appears under “Unpaid by Customers”. If the amount reaches the approval threshold, the invoice is saved but its journal is held until approved.

purchases.title: Record a Purchase
purchases.descriptionA: Guided step by step: supplier, goods, goods into the warehouse, then recording what you owe. Move back and forth as you like —
purchases.descriptionB: until you press “Finish & Save” on the last step.
purchases.learnMore: Learn about this: what a purchase is
purchases.savedHint: Everything was recorded together in a single save.
purchases.saveFailed: The purchase could not be saved yet.
purchases.goodsHintA: Quantity × purchase price here becomes the purchase value recorded as a
purchases.lineNotInStock: This item is not in the stock list yet, so it cannot be booked into the warehouse. Its purchase value is still recorded.
purchases.receiptCheckboxA: The goods have reached the warehouse — add them to
purchases.receiptHintA: Stock goes up together with its cost, which is later used to work out
purchases.receiptHintB: when the goods are sold. No extra journal — inventory already came in through the purchase journal.
purchases.overReceive: The quantity received exceeds the quantity bought.
purchases.fxCostHint: Stock cost is always recorded in rupiah, so the {currency} purchase price is multiplied by the rate you enter in the next step. Fill in that rate first if you have not.
purchases.detailHintB: owed to the supplier — money only leaves when the payment is recorded.
purchases.advancedDescription: Currency & rate, input VAT, and the purchase note.
purchases.inputVatHint: Posted separately to the input VAT account. Enter 0 if there is none.
purchases.noteHint: The item details from step 2 are carried into this note automatically, because a purchase is stored as a single amount.
purchases.receiptSummaryHint: Dated {date} — stock goes up, with no extra journal.

deliveryOrders.title: Delivery Orders
deliveryOrders.description: The document that ships goods. Issuing one reduces stock and recognises the cost of the goods that leave.
deliveryOrders.stockNoteB: (bags × kg/bag) when the delivery order is issued. Issuing is refused when stock is short.
deliveryOrders.emptyDescription: Create a delivery order to ship goods and reduce stock.
deliveryOrders.createDescription: Pick the consignee and (optionally) a source document, then set the goods and quantities (bags × kg/bag). Issuing the delivery order reduces stock in kilograms.
deliveryOrders.learnMore: Learn about this: what a delivery order is
deliveryOrders.noItems: Add at least one item before issuing the delivery order.
deliveryOrders.submitFailed: The delivery order could not be issued yet.
deliveryOrders.emptyStockDescription: A delivery order reduces stock, so the goods must already be on record. Record your first goods-in.
deliveryOrders.lineAvailableOver: Available {stock} {unit} — over stock, the delivery order will be rejected!
deliveryOrders.linePickItem: Pick an item to see its stock

returns.title: Returns
returns.description: Goods sent back — reversing part of an invoice or purchase along with its stock, receivable/payable, and VAT.
returns.noteA: A return is valued at the
returns.noteB: and may never exceed the quantity or value still outstanding. A sales return puts stock back in; a purchase return takes stock out.
returns.emptyDescription: Record goods sent back from an invoice or a purchase here.
returns.createDescription: Pick the original document, then set the goods and quantities being returned. Value and VAT follow the original document and may not exceed what is still returnable.
returns.fillOneLine: Enter a return quantity on at least one line.
returns.fillOneItem: Enter at least one line of returned goods.
returns.saved: The return is saved and journalled.
returns.networkFailed: Could not reach the server. Please try again.
returns.typeSales: Sales Return (goods back from a customer)
returns.typePurchase: Purchase Return (goods sent back to a supplier)
returns.effectSuffix: Valued at the rate of the original document.

consignees.title: Consignees ({count})
consignees.emptyDescription: A consignee is the party that receives the shipment at the export destination. Record the first one so it can be picked on contracts and delivery orders.

customers.title: Customers ({count})
customers.emptyDescription: A customer is the party you bill. Record the first one so invoices and receivables can be broken down per customer.
customers.taxExemptHint: Invoices for this customer default to no VAT (0%) — still changeable.
customers.saveFailed: Failed to save the customer. Please try again.
customers.updateFailed: Failed to save the customer changes

suppliers.title: Suppliers ({count})
suppliers.description: Open a supplier to record its purchases and payments.
suppliers.learnMore: Learn about this: how to record a purchase
suppliers.emptyDescription: A supplier is who you buy goods from. Record the first one so purchases and what you owe can be tracked.
suppliers.updateFailed: Failed to save the supplier changes
suppliers.emptyTxTitle: No transactions with this supplier yet
suppliers.emptyTxDescription: Record the first purchase or payment with the form above; the payable and its journal are created automatically.
suppliers.estimateTitle: This payment is not linked to any particular purchase, so the outstanding balance per document is only an estimate (the oldest purchase is settled first).
suppliers.introB: the goods arrive is recorded as a
suppliers.introD: an expense. The expense is only recognised when the purchase is recorded; this advance is then offset against that purchase to reduce what is still owed.
suppliers.outstandingHint: IDR base value of {count} advances with a balance left.
suppliers.unratedHintB: included in the IDR total on the left.
suppliers.noAdvances: No advances to this supplier yet. Record a payment up front with the button above.
suppliers.compensateHintA: Pick the purchase to reduce, then enter how much of each advance is used. Offsetting
suppliers.compensateHintB: value from Purchase Advances to what you owe the supplier — no further money changes hands.
suppliers.noTargets: This supplier has no purchase with an outstanding balance, so there is nothing to offset yet.
suppliers.unratedPurchaseRest: in foreign currency have no rate — their outstanding balance in IDR is unknown, so they cannot be offset yet. Enter the rate first.
suppliers.unratedNotShown: {count} foreign-currency purchases have no rate and are not listed here. Enter the rate first so they can be offset.
suppliers.allocLoadFailed: Failed to load the list of purchases.
suppliers.allocToastCleared: Allocation removed — the balance per document is estimated again
suppliers.allocToastSaved: Allocation saved. The journal is unchanged.
suppliers.allocPanelHintA: Changing the allocation only corrects the reported balance per document —
suppliers.allocPanelHintStrong: it does not change the journal
suppliers.allocPanelHintB: and moves no money. Left empty, the balance per document goes back to being
suppliers.allocNoPurchases: This supplier has no purchase with an outstanding balance, so there is nothing to allocate.
suppliers.noRateLine: A foreign-currency purchase with no rate — its outstanding balance in IDR is unknown, so it cannot be allocated yet.
suppliers.allocOverLine: More than this purchase still owes.
suppliers.allocOverTotal: The allocations add up to more than this payment.
suppliers.allocDeleteTitle: Remove every allocation on this payment?
suppliers.allocDeleteMessage: The balance per document goes back to being estimated FIFO, as it was before the allocation was made. The journal and the payment amount itself are unchanged.
suppliers.txOverAlloc: The allocations ({allocated}) add up to more than the payment ({amount}).
suppliers.txSaved: The supplier transaction is saved and journalled
suppliers.txEffectPayment: Reduces Accounts Payable and the cash balance
suppliers.txInputVatHint: Posted separately to the input VAT account.
suppliers.txAllocHintA: Pick the purchases this transaction pays. Left empty, the balance per document is merely
suppliers.txNoOutstanding: This supplier has no purchase with an outstanding balance.

ledger.title: General Ledger
ledger.pickAccountPrompt: Select an account to see its movements and running balance.
ledger.emptyDescription: Try widening the date range or picking another account. If there really is nothing yet, start by recording a cash transaction.
